string.text: Military cable

A cable designed for military operations. It is extra strong and resistant to impact and harsh environments, and may have added insulation and shielding to protect the signal from interference.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Capacitors

Electronic components that store electrical charge. They consist of two metal plates separated by a dielectric and are used to filter signals, smooth voltage fluctuations, and store energy.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Car battery

A power source for a car starter and other electrical systems. Usually lead-acid, it supplies high starting current and can power lights and the audio system while the engine is off.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Energy storage battery

A device that stores energy and releases it when needed. Types include lithium-ion, lead-acid, and nickel-metal hydride batteries. They are used in everything from mobile devices to electric cars.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Data flash drive

A common storage device: a flash drive with an SD card slot, compatible with all PDA models. It may contain data that interests traders.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A trader may be interested in this item.
Hard drive (1024 GB)

A 1-terabyte hard disk wrapped in an antistatic bag. With so much data, scientists no longer need to carry stacks of documents through the Zone: they can copy it to several drives and send them by different routes. At least one should reach its destination. These drives usually contain instrument readings.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A trader may be interested in this item.
Old pliers

Old, badly worn pliers with a handle wrapped in blue electrical tape and several notches on the jaws. They might bend something, but are awkward to use.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Magnet

A material or device that creates a magnetic field. Magnets are used in electrical engineering, medicine, and industry. Permanent magnets produce a constant field; temporary ones become magnetic only under an external field. Permanent magnets are common in motors, generators, and speakers.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Golden Star balm

Golden Star balm, made in Vietnam from camphor, menthol, mint, eucalyptus, and other essential oils mixed with petroleum jelly. Applied to the right spots, it helps with headaches, colds, runny noses, and insect bites. For external use only.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A trader may be interested in this item.
Military circuit board

An electronic circuit board designed for military equipment. It withstands harsh conditions such as high temperatures, vibration, and electromagnetic interference. These boards use high-quality components and undergo strict reliability and durability testing.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Old circuit board

An old, dusty circuit board wrapped in a bag. Its original device is hard to identify, but it is covered with assorted microcomponents. A soldering enthusiast might salvage a handful of capacitors and other useful parts.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Wire cutters

Cutters for wires, cables, and other materials, with durable metal blades and a comfortable grip. Over time the blades can become dull, making precise cuts harder, and the handle may lose strength and comfort.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Stalker map

A hastily drawn map showing trails, routes around anomaly fields, and extra notes. Up-to-date information is valuable in any form: a marked map, a PDA, or even a flash drive. It is usually bought by people working with the Informant.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A trader may be interested in this item.
Power bank

A power bank once used to charge mobile devices, now working poorly. Its indicators flash erratically and it charges devices very slowly or not at all. The internal battery or power controller may be worn or faulty. An electronics specialist or DIY enthusiast may still find it useful.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Power cord

A cable for connecting electrical devices to an outlet, with insulated wire and connectors at both ends. Its insulation can wear, crack, or expose the wire, creating a safety risk and causing power failures. Replace a damaged cord to keep the device working reliably.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Screwdriver

A tool for tightening and loosening screws, made of a steel shaft with a shaped tip and a handle for turning. The tip can wear down, especially after frequent use on hard materials or under heavy pressure. A worn or deformed tip makes the tool less effective.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Wires

Metal conductors used to carry electric current. They may be made of copper, aluminum, or other metals and covered with insulation to prevent short circuits and improve safety. Their thickness, length, and insulation vary by use.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A mechanic may be interested in this item.
Military dog tag

A personal item belonging to a fallen serviceman. Traders pay well for these tags, apparently reselling the identification details to the military. Why the military pays so much for a simple tag is unclear, but it does.
 
%c[0, 252, 186, 23] • %c[0, 156, 122, 39] A trader may be interested in this item.
